name: Mobile Friendly
description: Checks the viewport meta tag: present, width=device-width, and initial-scale=1. Mobile-first indexing is standard, and a correct viewport is the baseline signal of a mobile-ready page. It does not test real responsiveness.

scoring.summary: No viewport meta (name matched case-insensitively) => 0. Otherwise start at 3; content is split on ',' or ';' and each part on '=' (trimmed, keys lowercased). width != 'device-width' (case-insensitive): -1.5 if a width value is set, -1 if width absent. initial-scale absent/empty: -0.5; present but parseFloat != 1: -0.25. user-scalable=no/0, maximum-scale < 2 and ';' separators produce findings only. Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine.

rules.condition: settings.width lowercased === 'device-width' (content split on ',' or ';', keys lowercased)
initial-scale present and parseFloat(value) !== 1 (e.g. 1.0 is fine, 0.5 not)
score = max(0, score); the engine floors it to an integer

scoring.status_mapping: From the floored integer score: 3 pass, 2 warning, 0-1 fail. Examples: width=device-width, initial-scale=1 => 3 pass; device-width only => 2 warning; device-width + initial-scale 0.5 => 2 warning; initial-scale=1 only => 2 warning; fixed width + initial-scale=1 => 1 fail; fixed width, no scale => 1 fail; empty content => 1 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Find <meta name="viewport"> in the head. Static HTML / Vite: *.html / index.html. Astro: src/layouts/*.astro. Hugo: layouts/_default/baseof.html or partials/head*.html. Eleventy: _includes/** base layout. Next.js app router: Next adds a default viewport meta 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' automatically; override via export const viewport / generateViewport (or legacy metadata.viewport) in app/**/layout.tsx; pages router: <meta name="viewport"> in <Head> in _app (Next pages router also injects a default viewport if none). Parse content and apply the rules.

parity.note: Viewport is almost always a static literal in the head layout. Only framework-injected defaults (Next.js) and client-side modification are not directly visible; account for Next.js defaults explicitly.

fix_summary: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the shared head layout (index.html, Astro layout, Hugo baseof/head partial, Eleventy base layout); for Next.js app router export viewport = { width: 'device-width', initialScale: 1 } or rely on the default.

divergences.extension: Parts are split on ',' only and keys are case-sensitive, so 'width=device-width; initial-scale=1' scores as a fixed width with no initial-scale (1/3).
divergences.plugin: ',' and ';' both separate parts, keys and the device-width value are case-insensitive, and the tag name is matched case-insensitively. A ';' separator is reported as a finding without a deduction.
divergences.reason: Browsers apply such viewports (with a console warning), so the extension's score was a false positive.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded decimal score while the reported score is floored.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
